items.wrong: I like a table by the window.
items.fix: I’d like a table by the window.
items.why: To ask politely, use I’d like.

items.wrong: I’d like to eating the steak.
items.why: After I’d like, use a noun or to + base verb.
After will, use the base verb.

teach.goal: Como não traduzir palavra por palavra.
solo: Pergunte por que o erro acontece em português e como evitar.
group: Compare erro e forma natural: I like a table by the window. → I’d like a table by the window. | I’d like to eating the steak. → I’d like the steak. | She will has the fish. → She will have the fish..
Peça que digam a forma natural em voz alta.
extra90: Cada aluno cria um erro típico seu e o grupo corrige.

facts.label: Pedir e prometer
facts.sub: Peça com I’d like e ofereça com Would you like? Use will para o futuro: The food will be ready soon. She’ll have the fish.

facts.label: Eu queria
facts.sub: Para pedir de forma educada, use I’d like + coisa: I’d like a table. I’d like the steak. É mais educado do que I want. Use please no fim.

facts.label: Você gostaria
facts.sub: Para oferecer, use Would you like + coisa: Would you like a salad? Would you like some water? A resposta é Yes, please ou No, thank you.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: I’d like is a polite way to ask.
We say “I would to like a table”.
items.why: We say I’d like a table.

items.s: After I’d like, we can use a noun.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: I’d like is a polite way to ask. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
We say “I would to like a table”. → Falso (We say I’d like a table.)
After I’d like, we can use a noun. → Verdadeiro (Yes: I’d like a salad.)

paragraphs: It is Saturday night in a nice restaurant in Wellington. Soft music plays in the room. Dan comes in with a flower for his friend. A waitress named Tina meets him at the door. The room is warm and full of people. Tina asks about his table.
